source_name: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
source_reference: Norris et al., “Russian Nuclear Forces, 2001,” vol. 57, issue 3, pp. 78–79; submarine section
source_note: May 2001 assessment counts 17 operational SSBNs: seven Delta III, seven Delta IV, and three Typhoon boats. This is the full operational ballistic-missile-submarine count reported by the source.

source_name: Congressional Research Service
source_reference: Report RL31183, “China’s Maritime Territorial Claims: Implications for U.S. Interests,” CRS-31, issued 2001-11-12
source_note: The report states that the PLAN had no aircraft carriers. The statement covers the service’s complete carrier inventory at the report date, so zero maps directly to the scenario role.

source_name: Government of India, Lok Sabha
source_reference: Unstarred Question No. 2720, “Acquisition of Aircraft Carrier,” answered 2001-03-15, paragraph (a) to (c)
source_note: The Defence Minister states that the Indian Navy then had one aircraft carrier, INS Viraat, in service. The proposed indigenous ship was under construction and Admiral Gorshkov required repair and modernization before induction, so neither adds to the in-service role count.

source_name: Naval History and Heritage Command
source_reference: “U.S. Navy Active Ship Force Levels, 2000–2006,” row dated 9/30/01
source_note: The NHHC table records 12 carriers in the active force on 2001-09-30; FY 2001 Navy budget independently provides for 12. Inventory does not imply deployment or readiness.

source_name: Naval History and Heritage Command
source_reference: “U.S. Navy Active Ship Force Levels, 2000–2006,” SSBN row dated 9/30/01
source_note: The NHHC table records 18 SSBNs in the active force on 2001-09-30; FY 2001 Navy budget independently provides for 18. Inventory does not imply deployment or readiness.

source_name: French Senate
source_reference: Avis n° 90 (2001–2002), tome VIII, “Projet de loi de finances pour 2002 : Défense – Marine,” deposited 2001-11-22, section I.B
source_note: The Senate report calls Charles de Gaulle the sole carrier in service and estimates availability at about 60%. This is an in-service count, not a continuously deployable count.

source_name: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
source_reference: Norris et al., “French Nuclear Forces, 2001,” vol. 57, issue 4, July 2001, pp. 70–71
source_note: The contemporary assessment reports four French SSBNs in operation. It separately says three were maintained in the operational cycle; the count is fleet inventory, not the number on patrol or continuously ready.

source_name: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
source_reference: “British Nuclear Forces, 2001,” vol. 57, issue 6, November/December 2001, pp. 78–79
source_note: The contemporary assessment documents the four-boat Vanguard force. The fourth boat, HMS Vengeance, began its first deterrent patrol in February 2001. One-boat patrol practice does not reduce the fleet inventory count.

source_name: UK House of Commons
source_reference: Written Answers, 2000-03-17, “RN Vessels”
source_note: The Ministry of Defence identifies Invincible, Illustrious, and Ark Royal as the three carriers and says two are normally available for tasking. The 2000 roster is used as a near-year 2001 scenario estimate; readiness is not implied.
